name: raw-checksum
doc:
THE FIRST CAPABILITY CLAIM, now a regression guard: raw Checksum exists in client-go
and, since getwyrd/client-rust#6, in client-rust.

client-go serves rawkv.Checksum -- a SERVER-side crc64 over a key range
(kvrpcpb.RawChecksumRequest), returning crc64_xor / total_kvs / total_bytes. client-rust
had no such request type anywhere in its plan layer (rules doc RAW-4; roadmap 5.6) until
#6 added RawClient::checksum on the fork's `integration` branch (pinned from 385a1a3).
While it was missing, the Rust driver answered `unsupported`, a first-class, comparable
observation -- the driver must NOT emulate the feature (a client-side scan-and-hash
would checksum different bytes under different semantics and manufacture agreement out
of a workaround). Now it calls the method, and the upstream view, whose client-rust
still lacks it, keeps answering `unsupported` there.

So the claim surface is the CLASS: `ok` on both sides. The checksum numbers ride along
in both traces as evidence only -- crc64_xor and total_bytes cover the key bytes, run
prefix included, so they legitimately differ between the two runs of this comparison
and are never projected; comparing total_kvs is getwyrd/client-rust-test#89.

BOTH RUNS SHARE ONE SETUP: client-go writes the same three raw pairs in both; only the
CHECKER changes. Raw and transactional data are kept apart by construction (every key
lives under this run's unique prefix; no scenario mixes raw and txn ops on the same
keys; scenarios run serially) -- the APIVersion V1 caveat in kvrpcpb is about exactly
that mixing.

This diff vanished when client-rust gained raw checksum: ledger-check fired XCONVERGE
and G-0002 was re-stated as an `expect = "agrees"` regression guard -- the designed
lifecycle for a closed gap. A subject answering anything but `ok` here is a NEW GAP.

steps.why: Seed the range so the oracle's checksum is over something: an empty-range checksum would be a weaker witness that the capability actually ran.

THE CAPABILITY CLAIM. Both answer `ok` (with crc64/total_kvs/total_bytes as evidence in each trace): G-0002's regression guard. Until getwyrd/client-rust#6 the subject answered `unsupported`, and that class difference WAS G-0002.
